text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, extending a pullback from its peak earlier this week at $137.20. The decline came as U.S. crude oil prices dropped to $91.48 per barrel—down sharply from the geopolitical premium that had pushed the stock higher over the past few days. Though Middle East tensions remain acute (Iran fired missiles at Kuwait yesterday, and the U.S. is escalating sanctions with EU and South Korean backing), the immediate momentum has stalled, and with no fresh crisis breaking today, oil prices gave back some of their war-premium gains.

The broader refining environment remains supportive: diesel has hit record highs due to refineries in Ukraine and Russia being knocked offline, which typically benefits U.S. producers. However, that structural advantage isn't enough to prop up the stock when crude prices slip and geopolitical headlines stop generating fresh fear.
